items.claim: The unit's onset is carried by an English adversative and by a verse-initial particle the same row refuses to treat as a divider three times inside the span, and the second-person address that opens mid-span is left undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset verse's Hebrew is never spliced. That verse opens with a verse-initial particle: כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (web:Isa.9.1 = oshb:Isa.8.23, byte tier), while the row's scene-turn argument rests on the English “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish.” (web:Isa.9.1 = oshb:Isa.8.23), whose adversative has no counterpart token in the bytes. The identical verse-initial particle then stands at כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier), at כִּ֤י כָל סְאוֹן֙ (oshb:Isa.9.4 = web:Isa.9.5, byte tier) and at כִּי יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד לָ֗נוּ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier) — the three internal sites the row expressly declines to read as boundaries — so one particle carries opposite structural weight at the front seam and inside the span with no ground offered for the difference. Second, 'without a fresh subject or addressee' is contested inside the span: the next verse opens with a fresh nominal subject, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier); the one after turns to explicit second-person address, הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי ... שָׂמְח֤וּ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier), continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier); and the person does not resume in the birth clause, יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד לָ֗נוּ בֵּ֚ן נִתַּן לָ֔נוּ ... וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), whose verbs are third-person. Both witnesses render the address alike (“You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you” web:Isa.9.3 = oshb:Isa.9.2), and the splice deliberately avoids the doubled ketiv/qere token in that same verse. Everything else here verifies: the throne-name run פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖ד שַׂר שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier) re-collates against its cited verse; the doubled pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier) re-collates with the ketiv member correctly named as the unpointed medial-final-mem form (skeleton grade standing alone) and correctly refused as a special-letter seg; both in-span ketiv/qere sites (2 of the book's 49) and the exegesis note are disclosed; and the setumah keyed at oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7 matches the inventory under the correct type, tier-3 and single witness.

items.claim: The fresh-clause onset and the refrain close are byte-clean, but the supporting grammatical-role claim about Ephraim and Samaria is contested in both witnesses, as is its contrast with the preceding unit.
items.evidence: The onset run דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב (oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8, byte tier) is verse-initial and re-collates against its cited verse, and the closing refrain בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, byte tier) likewise; that refrain is byte-identical at five verses — web:Isa.5.25, oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, oshb:Isa.9.16 = web:Isa.9.17, oshb:Isa.9.20 = web:Isa.9.21, and web:Isa.10.4 (sweep: 5 verses) — so the digit and the named earliest site are both right. What the bytes contest is 'Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit'. The two names stand in apposition to the subject of a third-person plural verb: וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.9.8 = web:Isa.9.9, byte tier) — neither object nor addressee — and the folded English agrees, “All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria,” (web:Isa.9.9 = oshb:Isa.9.8). No second-person form occurs anywhere in this unit's five verses, from oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8 through oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12. In the preceding unit the second-person forms הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי ... שָׂמְח֤וּ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier) address the giver of the joy, while the royal figure there is third-person throughout, יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד לָ֗נוּ בֵּ֚ן נִתַּן לָ֔נוּ ... וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier). Both halves of the stated contrast therefore fail on the bytes, even though the onset itself stands. Disclosure is otherwise clean here: the front-seam setumah keyed at oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7 is named under the correct type (tier-3, single witness), and this span carries none of the 49 ketiv/qere verses.

items.claim: The stanza's only stated onset ground — that no fresh subject reopens — is contradicted by a verse-initial explicit subject in its own first verse and a second subject switch in the next, and the single tier-3 signal at this seam falls after that first verse rather than before it.
items.evidence: The unit's first verse opens וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא שָׁ֖ב (oshb:Isa.9.12 = web:Isa.9.13, byte tier): a verse-initial explicit nominal subject that is not the subject of the refrain clause it follows, where the subjects are אַפּ֔וֹ ... יָד֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, byte tier). The very next verse switches subject again, וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Isa.9.13 = web:Isa.9.14, byte tier), so the span opens on two consecutive subject changes; both witnesses render them so (“Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them” web:Isa.9.13 = oshb:Isa.9.12; “Therefore Yahweh will cut off from Israel head and tail” web:Isa.9.14 = oshb:Isa.9.13). Second, the parashah signal the row discloses is keyed AT oshb:Isa.9.12 = web:Isa.9.13 — the break falls after this unit's first verse — so the one mark anywhere near this seam groups that verse with what precedes rather than with what follows. The row records it as an interior break that does not move the close, which is true, without noting that it bears against the front seam it sits beside; tier-3, single witness, never a driver, and its absence would prove nothing either way. The close is byte-clean: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.16 = web:Isa.9.17, byte tier) is one of the five byte-identical refrain sites (sweep: 5 verses), and the span carries none of the 49 ketiv/qere verses.

items.claim: The refrain close and the mark disclosure verify, but the seam argument in the rejected alternative places the addressee shift a verse early and calls 'named' a class that neither witness names.
items.evidence: The close verifies: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.20 = web:Isa.9.21, byte tier) is one of the five byte-identical sites (sweep: 5 verses), and the setumah keyed at that same verse matches the inventory under the correct type (tier-3, single witness). The contested ground is 'the addressee shifts from the punished nation to a named class of officials after the refrain closes here': the following unit's onset verse supplies neither a name nor an addressee — ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי אָ֑וֶן (web:Isa.10.1, byte tier) identifies its targets only by what they do, and the English does the same (“Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees” web:Isa.10.1). The first second-person forms arrive one verse further on: וּמַֽה תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ ... תָּנ֣וּסוּ ... תַעַזְב֖וּ (web:Isa.10.3, byte tier) (“What will you do ... To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?” web:Isa.10.3). The row that argues the very same target calls it unnamed, so two descriptions of one seam disagree. Note also that this unit's own onset is a particle continuation, כִּֽי בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.9.17 = web:Isa.9.18, byte tier), which the row states honestly — leaving the whole front seam resting on the preceding bracket rather than on any onset signal in these bytes. The span carries none of the 49 ketiv/qere verses.

items.claim: Both seams, the type label and every disclosure object in this span are carried by the bytes: a verse-initial woe onset, a byte-identical refrain close, correctly typed marks at both edges, and no ketiv/qere or special-letter object owed.
items.evidence: The onset ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי אָ֑וֶן (web:Isa.10.1, byte tier) is verse-initial. The woe token occurs in 22 verses book-wide (sweep: 22 verses, skeleton), and this site belongs to the verse-initial oracle-onset class — a distinct object from the opening indictment, from the divine self-exclamation, from the invitation cry, and from the different lexeme that is never blended with it. The close בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (web:Isa.10.4, byte tier) is the last of the five byte-identical refrain sites — web:Isa.5.25, oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, oshb:Isa.9.16 = web:Isa.9.17, oshb:Isa.9.20 = web:Isa.9.21, web:Isa.10.4 (sweep: 5 verses) — so both the five-verse digit and the three-prior-stanzas digit hold, and the three prior sites carry their numbering space. Both parashah edges verify under the correct type and are disclosed: setumah keyed at the front-seam verse oshb:Isa.9.20 = web:Isa.9.21 and setumah keyed at the closing verse web:Isa.10.4 (tier-3, single witness). Of the 49 ketiv/qere verses and the 1 special-letter seg book-wide, none falls in this span, so nothing further is owed there. Holding the woe type while recording refrain-poem membership as texture keeps two frame objects unblended, which is what the bytes show: a verse-initial woe onset and a closing refrain meeting inside one four-verse unit.

items.claim: The span contains an undisclosed ketiv/qere site, and every seam claim in the row except the woe onset is argued from the English with no Hebrew form behind it.
items.evidence: The onset verifies: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט (web:Isa.10.5, byte tier) is verse-initial, a second woe onset four verses after the first. The disclosure defect is the next verse, which is ketiv/qere-bearing and staged as a doubled token pair, ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier for the spliced pair) — the ketiv member is unpointed in the staged bytes and is skeleton grade standing alone — while the row makes no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere; this book carries 53 such notes over 49 verses, the campaign's largest such inventory, and any span touching one of its verses owes the disclosure before slicing or counting there. On the substance, 'Assyria's own boastful self-assessment' is not what the span opens with: that same verse is first-person divine speech, אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ ... אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier) (“I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people who anger me I will give him a command” web:Isa.10.6), and the boast proper is framed only two verses later, כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (web:Isa.10.8, byte tier) — a frame form the row never quotes. The closing seam carries no spliced Hebrew at all, so the back boundary rests entirely on the English rendering of the rhetorical question at web:Isa.10.11. The parashah edges are correct and disclosed: setumah keyed at web:Isa.10.4 and at web:Isa.10.11 (tier-3, single witness).

items.claim: An in-span ketiv/qere site is undisclosed, the 'one uninterrupted response' ground passes over an intervening speech in the other mouth and a change in the divine party's grammatical person, and the closing remnant-object claim is made without a pointed form.
items.evidence: Both spliced onsets in the row verify against their cited verses. The disclosure defect: the second verse of this span is ketiv/qere-bearing, staged as the doubled pair ועתידתיהם וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier for the spliced pair) — the ketiv member unpointed, skeleton grade standing alone — with no ketiv/qere disclosure in the row. On the substance, the material between the two therefore-clauses is speech in the other mouth, opened by כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier) (“For he has said” web:Isa.10.13), and the divine party's grammatical person changes across those clauses: first person at אֶפְקֹ֗ד (web:Isa.10.12, byte tier) against third person with the stacked title at לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (web:Isa.10.16, byte tier) — both witnesses render the shift alike (“I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria” web:Isa.10.12 versus “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will send among his fat ones leanness” web:Isa.10.16). 'No addressee change between them' holds only because neither clause has an addressee at all, so the stated ground does not distinguish this seam from any other in the stretch. Third, the closing-verse remnant claim is asserted with no form: that verse opens וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.19, byte tier), which does exemplify the plain-noun object the row names, but a boundary-relevant claim on that root owes the pointed splice. Also undisclosed in-span is the suffixed divine epithet וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.17, byte tier) (sweep: 1 verse at this spelling), a different object from the title construct standing in the first verse of the next unit — so two title objects meet across this seam with neither side naming them. The parashah edges are right, including the petuchah keyed at the closing verse web:Isa.10.19 kept distinct from setumah (tier-3, single witness).

items.claim: The row's own remnant-object split misassigns the third verse of its span, the signature divine title standing in its first verse is engaged only through the English, and the throne-name collocation the row splices is left unremarked.
items.evidence: Both spliced runs re-collate against their cited verses, but the object assignment does not hold. The row places its third verse with 'the plain common noun' against its second verse's name-reactivating clause; in fact the two-token collocation שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier) stands at exactly three verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton) — as the vav-prefixed name form וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ (web:Isa.7.3, byte tier), at web:Isa.10.21, and as שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ (web:Isa.10.22, byte tier) — so web:Isa.10.22 belongs with the clause object, while the plain-noun object is what שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) exemplifies. The name form the whole argument leans on is never quoted, though the claim that this unit restates it is a claim about that form. Second, the unit's first verse carries the book's signature divine title, יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) (sweep: 24 verses on this construct spelling, one short of the staged 25-verse title census, the difference being a defective spelling outside this stretch), and the row engages it only as the English “the Holy One of Israel” with no divine-title object named — while the preceding unit's span carries the distinct suffixed epithet, so a title-object pair sits astride this front seam undisclosed on both sides. Third, the spliced אֶל אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier) goes unremarked although this collocation stands at exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton): here, and as one of the throne names at אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), where the accents differ so the identity is skeleton tier, not byte. That is a cohesion hook binding this unit to the one opening this stretch and it bears on the architecture the row proposes. Finally the back-seam claim names a divine-word formula without quoting it: the next verse reads כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (web:Isa.10.24, byte tier), a divine frame rather than a messenger formula in a human mouth, and a seam that leans on a frame owes the frame's owner. Marks at both edges are correct under their types (petuchah keyed before the span at web:Isa.10.19, setumah keyed at the closing verse web:Isa.10.23; tier-3, single witness), and the span carries none of the 49 ketiv/qere verses.
